Subject: Immediate runtime stabilization advisory — please run brief verification

Hi Chris / Acme SRE team,

We’ve identified a compatibility degradation affecting model streaming on a small subset of inference nodes that began at ~11:45 PST. The symptom is transient token drops for long streaming responses when the runtime kernel combo switches during autoscaling. We are putting an emergency stabilization patch into production now.

Action required on your side (takes 3–5 minutes):
- If you’re running a pinned model variant, please switch to the compatible fallback variant listed in the attached PDF and restart any long-lived sessions.
- If you rely on continuous streaming connectors, please pause new long-running streams for the next 30 minutes.

We will push a binary patch to the gateway and runtime (no change to your customer model artifacts). Ben will coordinate verification with your SREs; Marissa will own any billing/credits questions that arise.

Attachments: runtime_stabilize_instructions_v1.pdf (patch steps, smoke test checklist)

We’ll update in-line as soon as we see the patch finish rolling. Sorry for the short notice — this is an unscheduled emergency to prevent broader streaming degradations.

— Soojin

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 12:10 PM Chris Hogan <chris.hogan@acme-retail.com> wrote:
> Thanks Soojin — acknowledging.
>
> We see a minor uptick in 502s on streaming endpoints coincident with the timestamp you mentioned. Our team can perform the variant switch and restart sessions; can Ben paste the one-line CLI or API call we should run to switch the variant? Also confirm whether any rolling restart will cause request drops or whether requests will be transparently retried.

Hi Chris — quick instructions below (also in attached PDF):

CLI (recommended if you have the Redwood CLI installed):
rdwctl model variant-set --account=acme-retail --route=prod-streaming --variant=stable-v3

REST (one-liner curl):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/acme-retail/routes/prod-streaming/variant" \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"variant":"stable-v3"}'

Restart behavior: the runtime will drain live connections and try to complete in-flight tokens; any requests in-progress may receive truncated responses. We recommend a brief pause on new long-running streams during the switchover window (30 minutes). If you prefer, we can do a coordinated rolling restart where our runtime node is rotated out first to reduce truncation risk — let us know and we will schedule it now.

I’m standing by on Slack and phone if you want us to execute the variant switch for you. Once you confirm, run the smoke test checklist (attached) and post results here.

— Ben

Update and brief follow-up:

Patch rollout completed at 13:13 PST. We saw error rates return to baseline within 4 minutes on the affected nodes. Per Ben’s offer, our ops team executed a coordinated rolling restart for Acme’s prod-streaming route at 13:05 PST — that minimized truncated streams. Thank you to Chris and the SRE team for rapid coordination.

Next steps (postmortem follow-up):
- We will publish a short incident summary to the shared Drive folder by EOD (link above) with root cause and the permanent mitigation plan (kernel selection guard + additional pre-deploy smoke tests).
- We will schedule a 30-minute technical review with Acme’s platform team tomorrow to walk through the mitigation and to confirm there are no lingering session artifacts. Suggested window: Tue 2026-11-17 10:00–10:30 PST. Please confirm availability.
- Marissa will follow up with a billing note around any potential service credits for the disruption.

If you see any residual anomalies, please reply here or open the ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/45217.

Thanks again,
— Soojin
